heading: Does self-repair mainly come from mechanisms other than copy suppression?
definition: across the distribution, self-repair comes mainly from other sources (e.g. LayerNorm rescaling or other components), so copy suppression is a small part of it.
summary: Whether mechanisms other than copy suppression provide most compensation after ablation (“self-repair”) across the data distribution remains unestablished. Reported LayerNorm (layer normalization) contributions use a different total as their baseline, so they cannot establish copy suppression’s share of total self-repair.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: ?; 1-10B: ? for V6. Counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size shows coverage in these buckets, but no distribution-wide comparative attribution establishes the claim (arXiv:2402.15390#R1; arXiv:2310.04625#r14). Toy, 10-100B and >100B: no evidence in that counts key. Coverage that is not a test and lies outside that counts key (findings the verdict model filed as fitting no version, from groups sharing no authors with the original): <1B, GPT-2 Small IOI (arXiv:2608.19338#f0; arXiv:2610.02173#f0); 1-10B, three 7–9B instruct models on a factual task (arXiv:2610.02173#f2). Neither bucket moves from ? on this coverage.
suggested_status.reason: Counts: versions.V6.verdicts.supports.studies is 1, but the checker corrects that supports verdict to none. In GPT-2 Small/Medium/Large and Pythia 160M–1B, filtered and clipped LayerNorm contributions center around 30% of head direct effect for most models on many layers (arXiv:2402.15390#R1). This denominator is not total self-repair; the result establishes neither a majority contribution from other mechanisms nor a small copy-suppression share. R1 therefore cannot determine V6. Counts: versions.V6.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 1, so this study also cannot establish independent reproduction. The original reports that L10H7 and L11H10 jointly explain 39% of downstream self-repair after Name Mover ablation in GPT-2 Small on IOI (arXiv:2310.04625#r14), without distribution-wide attribution. These records do not establish V6's comparative claim. Coverage that is not a test: three findings bear on V6 and come from two groups whose author lists share no authors with the original (arXiv:2610.02173; arXiv:2608.19338). The verdict model filed them as fitting no version, so they carry no V6 verdict. (1) In three 7–9B instruct models on a factual task, final-norm rescaling accounts for at most 4.5% of recruitment under a dosed swap (arXiv:2610.02173#f2; arXiv:2610.02173#r11, arXiv:2610.02173#r12, arXiv:2610.02173#r13). This bears on V6's LayerNorm example. It is a share of recruitment under a dosed swap, whereas arXiv:2402.15390#R1 is a share of the ablated head's direct effect under resample ablation in GPT-2 and Pythia. (2) In GPT-2-small IOI, the conditional-backup interaction P×B (1.080 under mean ablation, 1.268 under zero ablation) is smaller than P×E in every tested lexical/order condition (arXiv:2608.19338#f0, no rows extracted). P×E, in margin change, is 1.830 under template-conditioned mean ablation and 1.681 under zero ablation (arXiv:2608.19338#r3, arXiv:2608.19338#r4). P is the 3 primary Name Mover heads, and E is the negative-name-mover pair 10.7 and 11.10. The authors rank group interactions and disclaim a complete circuit decomposition, and relative shares of self-repair are not quantified. (3) In GPT-2 Small IOI, several backup and name-mover heads are certified counterweights to the name-mover core in the clean model, with γ from −0.127 to −0.018 (arXiv:2610.02173#f0; arXiv:2610.02173#r2, arXiv:2610.02173#r3, arXiv:2610.02173#r4, arXiv:2610.02173#r5, arXiv:2610.02173#r6, arXiv:2610.02173#r7). None of the three jointly attributes total self-repair to copy suppression versus other mechanisms, and none is a V6 verdict, so the level stays ?.
suggested_status.open_questions: A distribution-wide joint attribution of total self-repair to copy suppression, LayerNorm, MLPs and other heads would determine whether other mechanisms dominate and copy suppression contributes a small share. Independent reproduction, sensitivity to token selection and clipping, and tests above 7B or on instruct/chat models would establish reproducibility and scope. V6 verdicts for arXiv:2610.02173 and arXiv:2608.19338, whose author lists share no authors with the original, would show whether their findings test V6 and in which direction; a test from either could move the level. arXiv:2505.17630 (within-head softmax redistribution, arXiv:2505.17630#f0), whose author list shares no authors with the original, is a further candidate from another group. arXiv:2307.15771 is a further candidate whose independence is unsettled: its author list is marked as sharing no authors, but a possible McGrath overlap with the original, raised in the completeness critique, has not been checked against the original's author list, so it cannot count as independent until that is checked.

source.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding a Motif in Language Model Attention Heads
source.authors: Callum McDougall; Arthur Conmy; Cody Rushing; Thomas McGrath; Neel Nanda

original_result.setup: The authors ablated the three Name Mover Heads, which copy names to the output, in GPT-2 small on the indirect object identification (IOI) task.
original_result.result: The two heads that lower token logits (“Negative Heads”), L10H7 and L11H10, jointly explained 39% of the compensation by later components after ablation (“downstream self-repair”). This measures their contribution in the specific task and intervention tested.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: LayerNorm scaling explained about 30% of a head’s direct effect on average.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Copy suppression's (L10H7's) share of self-repair on a distribution-wide sample, compared with LayerNorm and other components. This is the version's core clause 'so copy suppression is a small part of it'. arXiv:2402.15390 analyzes individual attention heads across models; its selected GPT-2 Small neuron experiment uses L9H11 (arXiv:2402.15390#R4), but this does not characterize all its ablations. No distribution-wide comparative attribution is reported. The original quantifies self-repair only on IOI (arXiv:2310.04625#r14).
untested.basis: Both studies' untested-parts lines; checker corrections for V6.untested[0] and arXiv:2402.15390#R1. R1 measures a LayerNorm contribution relative to head direct effect and cannot determine V6's comparative claim. counts: V6.studies_with_untested_parts is 2. V6.verdicts.supports.studies is 1 in the supplied counts, but the checker changes that verdict to none; it does not establish comparative coverage.

untested.what: Whether all sources other than copy suppression together form the majority of self-repair ('mainly'). LayerNorm is estimated relative to the ablated head's direct effect, not as a share of total self-repair (arXiv:2402.15390#R1). The final-layer MLP-neuron Anti-Erasure results establish its existence but do not measure its contribution to total self-repair (arXiv:2402.15390#R2, arXiv:2402.15390#R3, arXiv:2402.15390#R4, arXiv:2402.15390#R5, arXiv:2402.15390#R6). No row sums the sources or establishes their majority share relative to copy suppression.
untested.basis: The arXiv:2402.15390 untested line ('whether all other sources together form the majority, are not measured'). Checker corrections for V6.support[0] and arXiv:2402.15390#R1 identify the missing comparative attribution; V6.support[1] and its verdict fixes identify the unmeasured Anti-Erasure share. counts: V6.rows_by_state.cannot_determine 11; V6.rows_by_evidence_form.figure_only 9.

untested.what: Models above about 7B, toy models, and instruct/chat stages. Within the 1–10B range, Pythia-1B has self-repair and LayerNorm results (arXiv:2402.15390#R12), while Llama-7B appears in the neuron-frequency experiment (arXiv:2402.15390#R3). These results do not measure copy suppression's share relative to other mechanisms.

wording_issues.phrase: so copy suppression is a small part of it
wording_issues.issue: The only quantified copy-suppression share is from the original on IOI. There, L10H7 and L11H10 combined account for 39% of total self-repair after Name Mover ablation (r14), which the verdict fix reads as about 61% from other sources. That holds for one narrow task, with two heads counted together. No study gives a distribution-wide share for copy suppression.

wording_issues.phrase: self-repair comes mainly from other sources (e.g. LayerNorm rescaling
wording_issues.issue: For individual-head resample ablations on The Pile in GPT-2 Small/Medium/Large and Pythia 160M–1B, filtered and clipped LayerNorm/direct-effect averages center around 30% for most models on many layers (R1). This uses the top 2% of tokens by head direct effect and clipping to 0–100%; the denominator is the ablated head's direct effect, not total self-repair. No pooled cross-model average is stated. Neither the majority contribution of other mechanisms nor copy suppression's small share is measured. R1 therefore cannot determine V6 and warrants neither supports nor limits_scope.

The original quantifies the copy-suppression share of self-repair on IOI after Name Mover ablation (r14), without a distribution-wide attribution. arXiv:2402.15390 reports whole-sampled-dataset averages in Section 2.2/Figure 2 and entire-distribution LayerNorm ratios without clipping in Appendix A/Figure 10. Its approximately 30% LayerNorm/direct-effect estimate uses top-2% selection and clipping (R1; Figure 11). These unselected analyses do not jointly attribute self-repair to copy suppression versus other mechanisms, so the distribution-wide comparative claim remains unmeasured.

The studies use different measurements. The original measures downstream compensation of the IOI logit difference after three Name Mover Heads are ablated (r14), and examines directional dependence through projection interventions (r16). arXiv:2402.15390 measures direct-effect self-repair after individual-head resample ablations and decomposes it into downstream heads, MLPs and LayerNorm; its neuron experiments examine selected heads, including GPT-2 Small L9H11 (R4). It does not establish that none of the ablated heads is an upstream copier suppressed by L10H7. No joint measurement attributes self-repair to L10H7-mediated copy suppression versus these other mechanisms, leaving V6's comparative claim undetermined.

method_sensitivity.what: The LayerNorm estimate (around 30% of a head's direct effect) depends on keeping only the top 2% of tokens by direct effect and on clipping per-token percentages between 0 and 100%. The authors state that these choices materially affect the estimate.

method_sensitivity.factor: Ablation type (resample vs mean vs zero)
method_sensitivity.what: How often the clean-to-ablated LayerNorm scale ratio exceeds 1 differs between resample, mean and zero ablation, shown for Pythia-160M L11H2. This comes from a pack 'not in rows' line (Section 3.2, Figure 4), so no row backs it. The rows on V6 use resample ablation only.

method_sensitivity.factor: Direction of the upstream change (onto vs perpendicular to the unembedding)
method_sensitivity.what: In GPT-2 Small on IOI, Section 4.2 freezes LayerNorm scaling and projects upstream output changes onto or perpendicular to the IO unembedding. Most Backup Heads retain similar logit differences under perpendicular projection (r16). These interventions establish directional dependence; no revised allocation of self-repair shares under these projections is reported. The 39% allocation to L10H7 and L11H10 combined comes from the separate Section 4.1 Name Mover ablation (r14).

status_amendment.public_note: We now note findings from two research groups outside the original authors: one finds that final LayerNorm rescaling made up at most 4.5% of the compensating response in three 7–9B instruct models, and the other finds that on GPT-2 Small's indirect-object task the two negative heads interact more strongly with the main name-mover heads than the backup heads do. Neither finding was judged as a test of this claim, so its level is unchanged and it still can't be rated from the current evidence.
